title: Low's handwritten note: Hippler blames EMP from nuclear testing

Colonel Robert Hiper is saying that this was due to a, you know, an EMP fallout from a nuclear detonation,
tellings.difference: Comes through the 2025 Wall Street Journal article rather than Low's handwritten 1967 note.
tellings.link_reason: Both attribute the missile shutdown to Colonel Robert Hippler blaming EMP from nuclear testing or detonation.

plain: This story is about a handwritten note from 1967 and the Condon Committee, a scientific study of UFOs carried out for the US Air Force in the late 1960s. A former Air Force officer, Robert Salas, says a note written by Robert Low, an organiser of that study, records a talk with an Air Force colonel named Robert Hippler. According to Salas, Hippler told Low that the missile shutdowns of that time came from an EMP, a burst of electromagnetic energy, released by nuclear testing. Salas also names Roy Craig, another person on the study. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells the same thing, but he gets it from a 2025 Wall Street Journal article and not from the note itself. He says the colonel blamed EMP fallout from a nuclear blast. The story matters to its tellers because, if true, an Air Force officer was offering an ordinary cause for an event that the witnesses link to UFOs.
